**Ready for the maintainer to merge**

No `build.rs`, `.github/`, script or dependency changes, so it was built and tested normally. The branch already contains current `origin/main` (the trial merge was a no-op).

**What looks good**
- The one-mount law is applied at the right doors. Generation (`operation/job.rs:131`) refuses an op whose setup mounts a different machine or post than the active one, by name and with "activate 'SetupN' first". `verification_report` adds `program_problems`, so a program spanning mounts cannot post. A stale toolpath generated under another mount therefore cannot be posted after a switch. Machine limits are still re-checked live at post time, as before.
- `SetSetupMachine` and `SetSetupPost` snapshot `prev` and `next`, and both `apply` and `invert` are plain writes. Validation sits in the constructors, reusing `post::validate`, `is_sane` and the built-in machine lookup. A load of a v55 file refuses an insane per-setup machine by setup name.
- v54 migration is just the absent key. `a_v54_file_follows_the_document_mount_and_posts_byte_identically` covers 0 and 1 setups. v55 round-trip and undo are covered. A datum transfer carries the source mount.
- Click law: every node under a setup (WCS, Stock, Machine, Post, Fixtures, Tool list, Operations, and the Paste menu on the Operations row) calls `focus()` first. That queues an undoable `ActivateSetup`. Pages for an inactive setup (`setup_pages.rs: editable`) show "activate it to edit" instead of editors. The own/follow toggles and the Settings page act on the setup by name, not on the active one.
- The refactor is a move: `panes.rs` shrinks by about 640 lines. The moved browser code reads the same, and the existing browser tests were adjusted only for the new depth. New files are all under 400 lines, carry a provenance line, and have no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside tests.
- Snapshots (`egui_app`, `egui_tool_editor` read): only the per-setup tree shape differs (WCS G54, Stock, Machine, Post, Fixtures, Tool list, Operations). It is a decision doc per the Issue Law.

**Local results (merged with main, debug, own target dir)**

|---|---|
| app setup_mount | 6 passed |
| app setups | 11 passed |
| app setup_wcs | 7 passed |
| app one_wcs | 8 passed |
| app posting | 17 passed |
| app per_op_files | 9 passed |
| app project_roundtrip | 69 passed |
| app commands_undo | 32 passed |
| app golden_cl | 23 passed |
| app conformance | 6 passed |
| app machine | 32 passed |
| app setup_sheet | 7 passed |
| app fixtures | 14 passed |
| ui lib (CWD crates/ui) | 303 passed, 2 ignored |
| ui `--test egui_app` (CWD crates/ui) | 3 passed |
| clippy `-D warnings`, app + ui, all targets | clean |

**Requested before merge**: none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. A Machine or Post page for a setup that follows the document edits the *document's* mount, which every other following setup also uses. The selector under "Use the document's machine" can change several setups at once. Consider a one-line hint there. Own mounts are unaffected.
2. The Stock and WCS pages (`UiTarget::Stock` / `Wcs`) carry no setup name, and the Stock heading is just "Stock". If the user clicks another setup's radio while the page is open, it switches to the newly active setup's stock. This is consistent with "editors act on the active setup", but naming the setup in the heading would remove any doubt.
3. Fixture child rows and Operation rows (`Leaf::Model` / `Leaf::Op`) do not activate their setup. They edit by entity name, and generation refuses by name on a mount mismatch, so nothing wrong is edited.
4. `panes.rs` (1458) and `state.rs` (3812) were already over the ~400-line guide. Neither grew, and `panes.rs` shrank.
5. The GUI was not launched, as before. Snapshots were checked only on this OS.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
